# Lab 4.5: JSON Data Type & Functions

## What We Are Going to Do
Store data in the native JSON type and read it with field access, JSON_VALUE, JSON_QUERY, JSON_EXTRACT_ARRAY and LAX functions.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a table with a JSON column.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab04.events (id INT64, payload JSON);
INSERT INTO lab04.events VALUES
 (1, JSON '{"user": {"id": 7, "city": "Surat"}, "items": [{"sku": "A1", "qty": 2}, {"sku": "B2", "qty": 1}], "total": "450.5"}'),
 (2, JSON '{"user": {"id": 9, "city": "Pune"}, "items": [], "total": 120}');</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Read fields.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  id,
  payload.user.city AS city_json,
  JSON_VALUE(payload, '$.user.city') AS city_string,
  STRING(payload.user.city) AS city_typed,
  JSON_QUERY(payload, '$.items') AS items_json,
  ARRAY_LENGTH(JSON_EXTRACT_ARRAY(payload, '$.items')) AS item_count
FROM lab04.events;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Handle messy types with LAX functions.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT id,
  LAX_FLOAT64(payload.total) AS total_number,   -- works for "450.5" and 120
  SAFE.FLOAT64(payload.total) AS strict_number  -- NULL for the string "450.5"
FROM lab04.events;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[SQL] Flatten a JSON array.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT id, JSON_VALUE(item, '$.sku') AS sku, LAX_INT64(item.qty) AS qty
FROM lab04.events, UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(payload, '$.items')) AS item;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[CLI] Load newline-delimited JSON into a JSON column.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">echo '{"id": 3, "payload": {"user": {"id": 11, "city": "Delhi"}, "items": [], "total": 99}}' &gt; ev.json
bq load --source_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON lab04.events ev.json
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT id, payload.user.city FROM lab04.events'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Field access | `payload.user.city` returns JSON |
| `JSON_VALUE` / `STRING()` | Return a STRING |
| `LAX_FLOAT64` | Converts strings and numbers |
| JSON arrays | Flattened with `JSON_QUERY_ARRAY` + UNNEST |
